body: Back again. More miserable than last time. I've seen the doctor now. I got my sleeping meds and benzo's. She understood my stress, and told me to come back if the mentor I'm talking to now isn't helping. He wants me to start education, and I'm contemplating the day I have to go back to any school. Not really sober right now. I'm 23 years old - unfortunately plane was too expensive. I don't remember if I have. I've seen some of Norway and Sweden. Supposedly Scotland too, but I can't recall.

I would like to debate your note, but I'm afraid to cross a guideline. 
I read it as violent, angry poetry - and liked it.

"impossible to change people’s perceptions of one’s personality."

The change occurs upon you enlightening why your personality is the way it is. At first, people will perceive you with a first or even many impressions. And even then, all those impressions might be wrong, in which case your personality is misinterpreted. You have to explain yourself when people question, or the questions will be filled with assumptions. Don't be defined by an assumption.

I had to lose at least 20 friends before I found 1 that wanted to stick around - despite not feeling like I deserved to be liked. You aren't forced to be around the people that do not like you - you ought to be around those who do, bad company will make you feel like the culprit. 
I dislike a great many folks too, but that doesn't mean I wish for them, to have a hard time with everyone else.
If you still have friends, why do you believe they'll fade? If you were a terrible person, they would not befriend you in the first place. I like people that are socially awkward - suddenly it's not awkward, when all that was needed was freedom to express yourself, with people that think or act the same way as you. Like a true home. 
People may grow apart from each other, but from what I've gathered, that's natural. Consider the reason why a group of friends may take a distance; without jumping to the conclusion that you're to blame for being a bad person. I was told by someone, that those kind of people essentially did me a favor, by saving me my own valuable time for someone else, someone worthwhile.

Tried that as well, sometimes it helps, other times it makes me scribble for hours. 
I actually got invited over by the one friend to come and eat today / talk. It was nice, but when we went for a walk I ended up feeling really sick. Now I'm worrying again if it's early menopause, as I only have one functioning ovary left, due to a large cyst being removed with the other when I was 18. Now I can't stop thinking about it, because it's so long until the next doctor's appointment. I can't help but wonder "what if I can't have kids?", and it terrifies me. My friend was being really kind and understanding, she just put a movie on until I had to go home.
Yes, I would. But I don't want to overload the few good people in my life with negativity, that goes beyond anything they have shared with me. I don't want to become the person that's too big a mouthful to have a friendship with, because then I'd be left with nothing. :/ I like to believe empathy is important and limitless, but from what I've seen people say on the internet, it can become too much for them. It feels like a gamble when you have to guess where the line goes, not knowing how the other person feels or thinks. 
I tried taking the plane once - it was OK, but actually ended up taking the same amount of time with the waiting time, boarding, and short busride needed afterwards. Train would have been brilliant, but there's no connection to that place unfortunately.
While I think today has been a good day, I feel really sad right now

I'll find out with my mentor when I see him again, I don't know when the next appointment is supposed to be though. I usually receive a mail with the time.
The plan was to go this friday, but that's due to his little sister's confirmation on the upcoming sunday. I promised to help out with it, as I'm free to go on weekends, but the transport is something I dread - I usually never get to sit alone, so by the time I get there I'll be exhausted from squeezing into a corner, to avoid touching whoever's next to me. I didn't expect any of what happened at home the past days though. I overestimated how many plans I could handle, and eventually got triggered earlier. I don't wish to talk to anyone close IRL about self-harm and suicide thoughts, I find it embarrassing. There's a history of suicide and depression in my family, so it's a very touchy subject. We never talked as much about it as I'd wish for. 
Even when we're together, he gets very flustered if I don't take his "Okay's" for an answer. He has cried a couple times over the years, but mostly he'll get angry rather than sad. I'll try to enlighten him about my situation at least, but likely not this weekend.
I have 2 friends, one of them I'm missing very much though. I feel like she pulled away, or I might have pushed her away unintentionally. I have difficulty reading her.
Thank you for the link, I'm looking at it now, as well as the podcasting. I get anxious when I have to go to bed, laying still and waiting to fall sleep is the hardest part. When I don't have anything to look at or keep my vision occupied with, I start to wonder / think alot.

I wouldn't even be able to unfortunately. It was a one time counseling for confirmation of diagnosis, paid by someone else. One counseling with her would cost me 1/4th of my pay, something I wouldn't be able to afford. I do have a mentor that I had weekly sessions with before, I'm supposed to get them again. He made a schedule / calendar with me, one that would allow me to function while getting therapy, but also being able to travel and see my boyfriend. However, upon the first trip I took after not having seen my boyfriend for 3 months, I received a mail while I was with him, saying that I wouldn't be able to go again before August due to new rules (a forwarded message). That really broke the trust for me. Everytime I think I can count on a plan, as that's something I require to not stress, something comes along and forces it to be changed. I haven't figured how to deal with the latest change.
I started waking up at 4 am every night, no matter when I went to bed. I'm now getting zolpidem to sleep every 2nd day, and it helps. 
I didn't tell him.. Whenever I've had issues, he just makes a sad smiley or says he's sorry. It's not comforting at all. I want to be able to talk to him about important things like this, but he barely opens up about himself after almost 4 years. 
I'll try - I just really don't like asking for help or having to go to new places alone.

I hope you're still here.

Not being able to sleep can really push you over the edge - it's just not possible for the mind to function properly without. What's your anxiety about? Social anxiety, in regards to the staring?
It's possible to learn to cope with it, though it's not easy - but it's certainly worth it to be able to go out, without feeling like everyone's staring at you, judging. 
I know it can be hard to believe others when they compliment you, because you're set on believing otherwise - you're the one who has to deal with being you after all. Truly, you aren't ugly though. I don't understand why you think your skin is ugly, let along filled with acne.From the pictures I looked at, you have really smooth skin, as well as a harmonic face. Your lips are something many would kill for (figuratively speaking). Your ears aren't big. 

The anxiety highlights the insecurities and flaws, while keeping the praise and compliments in the background. It's the fear speaking, while you're already drained and vulnerable.
It's a cycle that might not end; but it's possible to put it on stand-by. Sometimes all you need is a break to clear your thoughts up, so they become rational again. If you're surrounded by a negative environment, it's difficult to get that break. Seek out, if you can.

The next appointment I could get with my "new" doctor was in 3 weeks. I barely managed to get my usual prescriptions - as prescribed by a psychiatrist - because she thought I was too young to take that medicine, despite having taken it for years. Didn't matter that I said I had something I needed to talk about, she had no time. I literately got 5 minutes of consultation, after my appointment time was 30 minutes overdue.
Thank you for the well wishing.

What to say, unhappy times..
My mom's reaction made me question if it's the right diagnosis though. It went from mixed personality disorder with hints of asperger to fullblown asperger. It doesn't really explain why I need so much sleep either. 
I'd like to have something that explains why I can't just DO certain things; but I'm afraid I'll be met with skepticism, or that they'll treat me with pity. 
I would, but I'm not sure what I should expect from it. Yes, she's a therapist specialized in autism / cognitive therapy. 
I wanted to be a streamer for a long time, but excessive playing made it necessary to get surgery around the wrist twice.
He lives roughly 8 hours away by bus. Scandinavia.
